Articles

Building plots

Preparing data for 3D layers

Read coordinate tables, join attributes by identifier, order grouped paths and convert a height matrix to a checked surface grid.

Choosing layers for observations and grids

Worked examples of points, paths, gridded surfaces, columns, distributions, intervals and reference geometry.

Scaling heights and facet ranges

Transform heights, label categories and dates, and control limits and z ranges across facets.

Building surfaces and solids

Worked examples of indexed meshes, function and fitted surfaces, density surfaces, level surfaces, hulls, solid glyphs and sweeps along curves.

Positioning groups and observations

Separate overlapping observations, align grouped columns and labels, and display stacked totals or proportions.

Displaying intervals and summaries

Plot supplied bounds on three axes and compute means, standard errors and quantile ranges for each cell of a grid.

Combining 2D and 3D graphics

Place ggplot2 panels on walls, stack slices in depth, draw terraced contours and arrange 2D and 3D plots.

Data types

Plotting angles and compositions

Place data in cylindrical, spherical, globe, ternary prism and quaternary simplex coordinates instead of a box.

Plotting maps and spatial data

Draw raster terrain, simple features and XYZ geometry, prism maps, profiles, flow arcs and space-time paths.

Reading and measuring meshes

Read mesh files, smooth, subdivide and simplify triangle meshes, measure curvature, and draw geodesic distances, paths and log maps.

Reading 3D scans and point clouds

Read textured meshes and point clouds from phone LiDAR apps, photogrammetry and airborne laser scanning, draw them, and rebuild a surface from points.

Drawing arrows and streamlines

Draw vector arrows, magnitude-scaled cones, integrated streamlines and solid streamtubes from a gridded field.

Slicing fields and point densities

Inspect gridded values on axis-aligned and oblique planes, add contours, and compare bandwidths for slices of a point-cloud density.

Drawing networks and trees

Draw igraph networks in three dimensions, multilayer networks on stacked planes, and dendrograms standing beside a heat map.

Appearance

Choosing camera views

Set camera angles, projection, framing and stereo output for static scenes.

Styling axes, legends and panes

Choose axis labels, align a colourbar with height, and style the panes and grids of a three-dimensional plot.

Lighting and styling surfaces

Control surface shading, use lighting presets and materials, and show the shading range in legends.

Output and sharing

Choosing rendering and image formats

Choose vector, raster, hybrid or traced rendering and save figures at the intended resolution.

Rendering volumes and traced surfaces

Trace signed distance surfaces, integrate scalar volumes and accumulate seeded path-traced images.

Rendering materials with path tracing

Render rough metals, glass, image lighting and participating media with the native path tracer.

Embedding plots in reports

Use knitr and Quarto to choose HTML viewers or static figures, supply alt text and compose panels.

Viewing plots interactively

Explore WebGL 2 scenes with tooltips, picking, selection, linked cameras and crosstalk filters.

Animating cameras and data

Render camera moves and camera paths, tween points and surfaces between data states, and hand the scene to the interactive viewer.

Exporting plots and scenes

Write model files, animated glTF, semantic SVG, TikZ and Asymptote, or pass scenes to rgl and rayrender.

Scientific examples

Drawing common charts in 3D

Worked plots of solid curves, distributions, covariance ellipsoids, streamtubes, cutaways and contour terraces alongside familiar charts.

Drawing ordination biplots

Draw site scores, variable arrows and grouped regions from principal-component and ecological ordinations.

Drawing tensor glyphs

Map symmetric positive semidefinite matrices to oriented ellipsoid or superquadric glyphs.

Drawing molecular structures

Read molecular coordinates, attach bonds by atom identifier and draw atoms and bonds in three dimensions.

Plotting colour gamuts in Lab coordinates

Sample sRGB colours in Lab coordinates and display their convex hull with interpolated vertex colours.

Mathematical examples

Constructing and reconstructing surfaces

Draw level sets from functions, reconstruct surfaces from point clouds and triangulate scattered height measurements.

Animating differential-equation solutions

Exact solutions of eight partial differential equations and a numerical magnetohydrodynamic solution drawn as surfaces that change over time with animate_3d().

Projecting four dimensions and drawing tilings

Project and rotate four-dimensional data, cut 4D meshes with a hyperplane, run a grand tour, and draw regular tilings and honeycombs.

Plotting curved spaces and spacetime

Draw data in spherical and hyperbolic geometry, the Hopf fibration, hyperbolic tree layouts, light cones, Lorentz boosts and Schwarzschild geodesics.

Drawing complex functions, knots and surfaces

Domain colouring on the Riemann sphere, Riemann surfaces of inverse functions, Möbius maps, torus knots and immersed surfaces with their self-intersections.

Viewing Thurston geometries from inside

Render an observer view in each of the eight Thurston geometries using intrinsic balls and geodesics.

Internals and extensions

How overlapping geometry is drawn

Explain how overlapping faces, lines and marks are ordered and clipped within a three-dimensional panel.

Writing a geometry extension

Write a new geom for coord_3d(): the scene packet it emits, how positions are normalised, and how register_geom_3d() connects it to the scene.
